image_spec.headline: Food waste makes up 58% of the methane escaping U.S. landfills.
image_spec.body: Food breaks down faster than most trash, so it gives off methane early.
image_spec.tip: Eat it or freeze it. Both count.

posts.caption:
Here's one that surprised us. About 58% of the methane escaping U.S. landfills comes from food waste, according to the EPA.

Food breaks down faster than most of what ends up in there, so it gives off that gas early. That's the part of a forgotten bag of spinach nobody really thinks about.

The fix is pretty unglamorous. Eat the leftovers this week, and freeze what you won't get to. 🧊

Save this one for Friday, when the fridge is packed.

#smartshopping #groceryshopping #familymeals #stashsmart #mobilepantry
posts.source_note: U.S. EPA Office of Research and Development, Quantifying Methane Emissions from Landfilled Food Waste (Oct 2023): an estimated 58% of fugitive methane emissions (those not captured by landfill gas collection) from municipal solid waste landfills are from landfilled food waste; food decays faster than other landfilled materials. https://www.epa.gov/land-research/quantifying-methane-emissions-landfilled-food-waste
